claims.text: GDACS's report for this event (event ID VO 1000148) rates the Krakatau eruption an Orange alert, "unlikely to require external humanitarian assistance based on the exposed population and coping capacity," with about 2,000 people within 30km and no people affected within 100km; it records a Volcanic Explosivity Index of 6 for the episode, running from 04 Sep 2026 21:00 UTC to 05 Sep 2026 14:30 UTC. Re-checked 1 November 2026: the report page is unchanged, still showing episode 2 as the latest and no updated exposure or casualty figures; geologi.esdm.go.id could not be reached to confirm the press-reported Level III status.

Indonesia's Badan Geologi (PVMBG), in its update on Gunung Anak Krakatau dated 7 September 2026, states the volcano's activity level remains at Level III / Siaga ("tingkat aktivitas G. Anak Krakatau tetap pada Level III (Siaga)"), maintains the 3km exclusion zone around the volcano's center barring residents and visitors/tourists/climbers from entering ("radius 3 km dari pusat aktivitas G. Anak Krakatau"), records 3 Strombolian eruptions after the continuous eruption episode ended ("3 kali erupsi Strombolian terjadi setelah episode erupsi menerus berakhir") alongside 9 emission and 93 low-frequency earthquakes, and assesses that "the probability of an eruption occurring in the coming period is still high" ("Probabilitas untuk terjadi letusan dalam beberapa periode waktu selanjutnya adalah masih tinggi").

Indonesia's Badan Geologi (PVMBG), in its update on Gunung Anak Krakatau dated 11 September 2026 (evaluation as of 06:00 WIB), states the volcano's activity level remains at Level III / Siaga ("tingkat aktivitas G. Anak Krakatau tetap pada Level III (Siaga)") with the 3km exclusion zone unchanged, and records 14 Strombolian eruptions since the continuous eruption episode ended ("telah terjadi 14 kali erupsi Strombolian"), up from 3 as of 7 September; it assesses the probability of a further eruption in the coming period as still high, and notes deep volcanic earthquakes show an increasing trend while shallow volcanic seismicity is fluctuating with a declining tendency.

Indonesia's Badan Geologi (PVMBG), in a Special Report (Laporan Khusus) dated 21 September 2026, downgraded Gunung Anak Krakatau's activity level from Level III (Siaga) to Level II (Waspada), effective 21 September 2026 at 18:30 WIB ("terhitung mulai tanggal 21 September 2026 pukul 18.30 WIB"), and reduced the exclusion zone from 3km to 2km from the volcano's center ("tidak diperbolehkan memasuki dan melakukan kegiatan di dalam wilayah radius 2 km"). It cites declining seismicity on 20 September ("1 kali Gempa Low Frequency dan Tremor Menerus dengan rata rata amplitudo 2 mm") and a deflation trend in deformation monitoring supporting the downgrade, and asks residents of the Banten and Lampung coasts to stay calm and not believe rumors of an eruption ("jangan mempercayai isu-isu tentang erupsi").

Detik.com's report (published 11 October 2026, 18:53 WIB, observation window 12:00-18:00 WIB and attributed to PVMBG observer Muhammad Dika Nurzaman) states Gunung Anak Krakatau remains at Alert Level III (Siaga), with a mandatory exclusion zone of 5km from the eruption center plus 1km around new islands in the northwest and southeast sectors. Multiple other Indonesian outlets (Kompas, Warta Ekonomi, IDN Times, RRI) separately report Badan Geologi/PVMBG raised the volcano from Level II (Waspada) back to Level III effective 9 October 2026, 21:00 WIB, citing report number 1729.Lap/GL.03/BGL/2026 and a cluster of 13 eruptions recorded by 21:20 WIB that evening, following a run of eruptions on 5 and 8 October while the volcano was still at Level II; none of these figures have been independently confirmed via Badan Geologi's own geologi.esdm.go.id site, which did not return the relevant bulletin to direct requests during this check.

The Government of Lampung Province's notice published on 4 November 2026 reports a disaster-preparedness meeting involving BPBD, PVMBG and BMKG. BPBD head Aswarodi states that Anak Krakatau remains at Level III (Siaga) and advises residents, fishers and tourists to stay at least 5km from the crater. This provincial statement supports the status and safety advice as of 4 November; it does not establish the October escalation date, the additional island exclusion zone reported by the press, or continuous eruption through the retrieval date.

description: Indonesia's Krakatau volcano, in the Sunda Strait, began an eruption on 4 September 2026 that GDACS classified under an Orange alert. PVMBG downgraded it to Level II on 21 September; Indonesian press subsequently reported a return to Level III on 9 October. Lampung's provincial government reported Level III (Siaga) and advised a 5km exclusion radius on 4 November. The precise October escalation date and additional restrictions around new islands remain supported only by unverified press reporting in this record.

impact.summary: Casualty and displacement totals are not established in the cited evidence. Lampung's 4 November notice reports Level III (Siaga) and advises residents, fishers and tourists to remain at least 5km from the crater.

event.scale: GDACS Orange alert; Level III (Lampung, 4 Nov)

name: Volcanic Eruption — Krakatau, Indonesia

updates.text: Lampung's provincial government reports Anak Krakatau at Level III (Siaga), with advice to stay at least 5km from the crater. The notice supports those conditions on 4 November, without establishing the date of the October escalation.

Indonesian press widely report Badan Geologi (PVMBG) raised Gunung Anak Krakatau from Level II (Waspada) back to Level III (Siaga) effective 9 October 2026, 21:00 WIB, after a cluster of eruptions, widening the exclusion zone from 2km to 5km plus 1km around new islands; still reported at Level III as of 11 October, though not yet corroborated on PVMBG's own site.

Indonesia's Badan Geologi (PVMBG) downgraded Gunung Anak Krakatau from Alert Level III (Siaga) to Level II (Waspada), effective 21 September 2026 18:30 WIB, citing declining seismicity and a deflation trend in ground deformation, and reduced the mandatory exclusion zone from 3km to 2km around the crater.

Indonesia's Badan Geologi (PVMBG) reported 14 Strombolian eruptions since the continuous episode ended, as of 11 September, up from 3 recorded on 7 September; the volcano remains at Alert Level III (Siaga) with the 3km exclusion zone unchanged, and the probability of a further eruption remains assessed as high.

Indonesia's Badan Geologi (PVMBG) confirmed the volcano remains at Alert Level III (Siaga) with a 3km exclusion zone as of 7 September, following three Strombolian eruptions after the initial 25-hour continuous episode ended, and assessed the probability of a further eruption in the coming period as still high.
